_ratchet_note: The ratchet was 24 and is now 27, and the increase is the guard learning to see rather than a regression. Its marker window was a fixed 3-line lookbehind, which misread two of the three suites' own conventions: apcore-rust writes the clause id on a `// clause:` line ABOVE the attribute block, so EVERY `#[ignore]`d clause in that SDK was reported LIVE — a false negative in exactly the direction the guard exists to catch — and apcore-python writes a six-line `@pytest.mark.skip(reason=...)` above the `def` whose docstring carries the id, further than three lines reach. The window is now item-scoped. Five asymmetries the corrected guard exposed were FIXED rather than accepted (see the CHANGELOG entry); the 27 below were each checked against the SDK source on the date in their note.

acl_system.add_rule.error.value_error_kw.note: verified 2026-09-21: the kwargs form of add_rule is Python-only by spec (D10-006); apcore-typescript and apcore-rust take a prebuilt rule object. Real API shape, not a gap.

call_chain_guard.guard_call_chain.input..note: verified 2026-09-21: a required parameter is compile-enforced in TypeScript, so there is no runtime arity rejection to assert. apcore-python and apcore-rust reject at runtime because a caller can reach them untyped.

decorator_bindings.load_bindings.error.B.note: verified 2026-09-21: apcore-rust resolves handlers from a statically-typed handler map at compile time and cannot import a named callable from a string, so the error has no reachable trigger.
verified 2026-09-21: apcore-rust treats `target` as an opaque handler-map key and performs no ':' shape validation; there is no parse step to fail.
verified 2026-09-21: apcore-rust handlers are statically-typed closures — a non-callable cannot be registered, so the runtime check the other two need does not exist.

decorator_bindings.module.error.FUNC_MIS.note: verified 2026-09-21: signature inference is Python-only. The FUNC_MISSING_RETURN_TYPE code exists in all three registries but only apcore-python has an inference step that can raise it.
verified 2026-09-21: same as FUNC_MISSING_RETURN_TYPE — the code is declared everywhere, the inference step that raises it is Python-only.

decorator_bindings.module.input.func_or_.note: verified 2026-09-21: apcore-rust has no decorator and no runtime type-hint inference; a module declares its schemas explicitly.

event_system.deliver.error.ImportError_a.note: verified 2026-09-21: Python raises ImportError when aiohttp is absent. apcore-typescript uses global fetch and apcore-rust gates the HTTP path behind the `events` cargo feature at compile time, so neither has an import to fail.

event_system.deliver.error.WEBHOOK_DELIV.note: verified 2026-09-21: only apcore-python defines DeliveryError/WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_FAILED; apcore-typescript has no such type and apcore-rust returns ModuleError(General*). This is the D-92 shape (a declared error type not every SDK defines) and is the one entry here worth raising as a decision rather than accepting as a language difference.

event_system.emit.input.event_type.not_e.note: verified 2026-09-21: emit() is fire-and-forget in apcore-typescript and apcore-rust and validates nothing; the rule is unenforceable as a rejection contract there. Caller precondition.

event_system.on_failure.input.subscriber.note: verified 2026-09-21: apcore-typescript's CircuitBreakerWrapper and apcore-rust's CircuitBreaker are per-subscriber objects, so there is no subscriber_id parameter to require.

event_system.subscribe.input.subscriber..note: verified 2026-09-21: a Python-only runtime TypeError guard; apcore-typescript enforces EventSubscriber statically and apcore-rust via Box<dyn EventSubscriber>.

module_interface.execute.input.execute.m.note: verified 2026-09-21: `execute` is a required trait method in apcore-rust — a type without it does not compile, so there is no runtime descriptor check to mirror.

multi_module_discovery.discover_multi_cl.note: verified 2026-09-21: apcore-rust's derive_module_ids is pure and never opens the file, so a nonexistent path cannot raise MODULE_LOAD_ERROR (D11-004).

verified 2026-09-21: same as pre_approval_hook.allow — Python-only safety hook (D-30).
